key_violations.original: 1. Your firm failed to have, for each batch of medical gas, appropriate laboratory determination of satisfactory conformance to final specifications for the medical gas, including the identity and strength of each active ingredient, prior to release (21 CFR 213.165(a)). 1 Your firm is a manufacturer of Oxygen, USP for administration by inhalation, including for use in hospital settings. Your firm failed to adequately test finished batches of your medical gases for the identity and strength of your active ingredients (Oxygen, USP) before release and distribution, which includes using properly calibrated instruments. For example, while reviewing an investigation into a customer complaint for a medical gas mix-up, our investigator identified that your filling technician reported passing testing results for batches of Oxygen, USP prior to their release without actually performing the required tests. The customer complaint revealed that third-party testing of the Oxygen, USP batches showed the presence of (b)(4) as high as 99% within the containers. A container labeled as medical oxygen administered to a patient despite having a level of 99% (b)(4) (and less than 1% oxygen) represents a catastrophic, immediately life-threatening event from complete oxygen deprivation.
key_violations.description: 1. 귀사는 각 의료용 가스 배치에 대해 출하 전에 각 유효성분의 확인(identity)과 함량(strength)을 포함하여 최종 규격에 대한 적합성을 적절한 시험으로 확인하지 않았다(21 CFR 213.165(a)). 1 귀사는 병원 환경 사용을 포함한 흡입 투여용 Oxygen, USP 의 제조업체다. 귀사는 출하·유통 전에 의료용 가스 완제품 배치의 유효성분(Oxygen, USP) 확인과 함량을 적절히 교정된 기기를 사용하는 것을 포함하여 적절히 시험하지 않았다. 예를 들어 의료용 가스 혼입에 관한 고객 불만 조사를 검토하던 중, 조사관은 충전 기술자가 요구된 시험을 실제로 수행하지 않고 출하 전 Oxygen, USP 배치의 적합 시험 결과를 보고한 사실을 확인했다. 고객 불만에서는 해당 Oxygen, USP 배치에 대한 제3자 시험 결과 용기 안에 (b)(4) 가 최대 99% 존재한 것으로 드러났다. 의료용 산소로 표시된 용기가 (b)(4) 99%(산소 1% 미만) 수준인 채로 환자에게 투여되는 것은 완전한 산소 결핍으로 즉시 생명을 위협하는 재앙적 사건이다.
key_violations.risk: 산소가 아닌 가스가 의료용 산소로 출하돼 환자가 즉시 산소 결핍으로 사망할 수 있다.

key_violations.original: 2. Your firm failed to test samples of each incoming designated medical gas for identity and conformity with all appropriate written specifications for purity, strength, and quality. Your firm also failed to validate and establish the reliability of your incoming designated medical gas supplier’s test analyses at appropriate intervals (21 CFR 213.82(a) and 213.82(b)). 2 Your firm failed to conduct identity testing for each incoming designated medical gas (DMG) lot used in medical gas manufacturing, including Oxygen, USP. Additionally, you relied on your supplier’s certificates of analysis (COA) of your incoming DMG without establishing the reliability of your supplier’s test analyses at appropriate intervals.
key_violations.description: 2. 귀사는 입고되는 각 지정 의료용 가스(DMG)의 시료에 대해 확인(identity) 시험과 순도(purity)·함량(strength)·품질(quality)에 관한 모든 적절한 서면 규격에의 적합성 시험을 하지 않았다. 또한 입고 DMG 공급업체 시험분석의 신뢰성을 적절한 주기로 검증·확립하지 않았다(21 CFR 213.82(a) 및 213.82(b)). 2 귀사는 Oxygen, USP 를 포함하여 의료용 가스 제조에 사용한 입고 DMG 각 로트에 대해 확인시험을 하지 않았다. 또한 공급업체 시험분석의 신뢰성을 적절한 주기로 확립하지 않은 채 입고 DMG 에 대해 공급업체의 시험성적서(COA)에 의존했다.
key_violations.risk: 입고 가스의 정체를 확인하지 않아 오충전·혼입이 출하 단계까지 걸러지지 않는다.

key_violations.original: 3. Your firm failed to establish and follow adequate written procedures describing the handling of all written and oral complaints regarding a medical gas, including provisions for review by the quality control unit of any complaint involving the possible failure of a medical gas to meet any of its specifications and, for such medical gas, a determination as to the need for an investigation in accordance with 21 CFR 213.192 (21 CFR 213.198(a)). 3 A hospital contacted your firm in October 2025 to report the presence of (b)(4) in containers of Oxygen, USP that you filled and distributed to them. You stated to our investigator that you told the complainant it was impossible to have (b)(4) in the oxygen tank and subsequently failed to document and investigate the incident in a timely manner per your complaint handling procedure. It was not until after the complainant conducted third-party testing on the contents of the containers and sent you a termination of services letter on November 20, 2025, that you initiated an investigation into the complaint. Your firm’s investigations into the errant Oxygen, USP containers were deficient. Your firm’s investigations revealed that the errant Oxygen, USP containers were filled with (b)(4) during repair by a third party, but upon receipt by your firm, your filling technician failed to test the lot as required. However, your investigations did not consider other containers repaired by the third party; other Oxygen, USP batches that may be affected by the incident; or remediations beyond employee termination and additional employee training.
key_violations.description: 3. 귀사는 의료용 가스에 관한 모든 서면·구두 불만의 처리를 기술한 적절한 서면 절차를 수립·준수하지 않았다. 여기에는 의료용 가스가 규격을 충족하지 못했을 가능성이 있는 모든 불만에 대한 품질관리부서의 검토와, 해당 가스에 대해 21 CFR 213.192 에 따른 조사 필요성 판단 규정이 포함된다(21 CFR 213.198(a)). 3 2025년 10월 한 병원이 귀사가 충전·공급한 Oxygen, USP 용기에 (b)(4) 가 존재한다고 귀사에 알렸다. 귀사는 조사관에게 산소 탱크에 (b)(4) 가 있을 수 없다고 불만 제기자에게 말했다고 진술했고, 이후 불만 처리 절차에 따라 적시에 그 사건을 문서화하고 조사하지 않았다. 불만 제기자가 용기 내용물에 대한 제3자 시험을 하고 2025년 11월 20일 서비스 계약 해지 서한을 보낸 뒤에야 귀사는 불만 조사를 시작했다. 문제의 Oxygen, USP 용기에 대한 귀사의 조사는 부실했다. 조사 결과 그 용기는 제3자의 수리 과정에서 (b)(4) 로 충전됐는데, 귀사가 받은 뒤 충전 기술자가 요구된 대로 그 로트를 시험하지 않은 것으로 드러났다. 그러나 귀사의 조사는 그 제3자가 수리한 다른 용기, 그 사건의 영향을 받았을 수 있는 다른 Oxygen, USP 배치, 또는 직원 해고와 추가 교육 이상의 시정조치를 고려하지 않았다.
key_violations.risk: 불만 조사가 단건·개인 책임으로 끝나 같은 원인의 다른 용기·배치가 시장에 남을 수 있다.

key_violations.original: 4. Your firm’s quality unit failed to exercise its responsibility to ensure medical gases are manufactured in compliance with CGMP, and meet established specifications for identity, strength, quality, and purity (21 CFR 213.22). 4 Your firm failed to establish an adequate quality unit (QU) with the responsibilities and authority to oversee the manufacture of medical gases. For example, you failed to ensure: Assignment of an adequate QU with sufficient responsibilities and authorities (213.22(a)). Establishment of appropriate written procedures for medical gas manufacturing (213.22(c)). Personnel training in CGMP requirements with sufficient frequency (213.25(a)).
key_violations.description: 4. 귀사의 품질부서는 의료용 가스가 CGMP 에 따라 제조되고 확인(identity)·함량(strength)·품질(quality)·순도(purity)에 관한 설정 규격을 충족하도록 보장할 책임을 이행하지 않았다(21 CFR 213.22). 4 귀사는 의료용 가스 제조를 감독할 책임과 권한을 갖춘 적절한 품질부서(QU)를 수립하지 않았다. 예를 들어 귀사는 다음을 보장하지 못했다: 충분한 책임과 권한을 가진 적절한 QU 의 지정(213.22(a)). 의료용 가스 제조를 위한 적절한 서면 절차의 수립(213.22(c)). 충분한 빈도의 CGMP 요건 교육(213.25(a)).
key_violations.risk: 품질부서가 실질적으로 존재하지 않아 출하·불만·교육 관리 전반이 통제되지 않는다.

deep_analysis.fda_evaluation: FDA 는 2026년 4월 15일 483 회신을 검토했다. 업체는 4개 위반 모두에 대해 새 시설 이전에 맞춰 시험·출하, 입고 가스 관리·공급업체 적격성 평가, 불만·CAPA, 품질관리·교육 SOP 를 개발 중이며 충전 기록에 2인 확인을 추가하겠다고 했으나, FDA 는 Oxygen, USP 완제품 규격과 시험·출하 절차, 시험기기 교정 증거, 품질 특성을 충족함을 보여주는 시험 결과를 제시하지 않았고, 영향받았을 수 있는 다른 배치로의 조사 확대와 다른 결함 원인 검토, 적절한 CAPA 계획의 세부 내용도 없으며, QU 감독과 직원 교육을 보장하는 시정조치의 근거가 부족하다며 모두 불충분하다고 평가했다.

required_remediation.deadline: 서한 수령 후 15영업일 이내 서면 회신(CDER-OC-OMQ-Communications@fda.hhs.gov)
items: 배치 처분 결정 전 사용하는 모든 시험법·규격과 관련 절차 목록, 시험실 체계에 대한 독립적 종합 평가와 개선 계획을 제출한다.
DMG·용기·마개 공급업체 적격성과 입고 DMG 로트별 확인시험·COA 신뢰성 검증 체계를 포함한 자재 시스템 검토와 CAPA 를 제출한다.
최근 3년간 중요 조사 전반에 대한 독립적 소급 검토와 CAPA 프로그램 평가·개선 계획을 제출한다.
데이터 무결성 조사·위험평가·관리 전략을 수립하고, 미국 시장용 의료용 가스 제조 지속 여부를 밝힌다.

deep_analysis.administrative_risks: 미해결 위반은 다른 연방기관의 계약 수주를 막을 수 있고 수출증명서 발급 보류로 이어질 수 있다. 위반이 완전히 해소되고 CGMP 준수가 확인될 때까지 이 업체를 제조소로 기재한 신규 신청·변경 승인이 보류될 수 있으며, 시정 확인을 위한 재실사가 이뤄질 수 있다.

violations_ko.statement_ko: 귀사는 각 의료용 가스 배치에 대해 출하 전에 각 유효성분의 확인(identity)과 함량(strength)을 포함하여 의료용 가스 최종 규격에 대한 적합성을 적절한 시험으로 확인하지 않았다 (21 CFR 213.165(a)).

귀사는 입고되는 각 지정 의료용 가스의 시료에 대해 확인(identity) 시험과 순도(purity)·함량(strength)·품질(quality)에 관한 모든 적절한 서면 규격에의 적합성 시험을 하지 않았다. 또한 입고 지정 의료용 가스 공급업체 시험분석의 신뢰성을 적절한 주기로 검증·확립하지 않았다 (21 CFR 213.82(a) 및 213.82(b)).
귀사는 의료용 가스에 관한 모든 서면·구두 불만의 처리를 기술한 적절한 서면 절차를 수립·준수하지 않았다. 여기에는 의료용 가스가 규격을 충족하지 못했을 가능성이 있는 불만에 대한 품질관리부서의 검토와, 해당 가스에 대해 21 CFR 213.192 에 따른 조사 필요성 판단 규정이 포함된다 (21 CFR 213.198(a)).
귀사의 품질부서는 의료용 가스가 CGMP 에 따라 제조되고 확인(identity)·함량(strength)·품질(quality)·순도(purity)에 관한 설정 규격을 충족하도록 보장할 책임을 이행하지 않았다 (21 CFR 213.22).

8632153aa053.source_text: FDA Inspection Violations were identified and documented during an inspection of your drug manufacturing facility, Conroe Welding Supply, Inc., FDA Establishment Identifier (FEI) 1625647, at 4425 North Frazier Street, Conroe, from March 30 to April 3, 2026. This inspection was conducted under FDA’s statutory authority and public health responsibilities to protect the public from unsafe, ineffective, and poor quality drugs, including medical gases. This warning letter summarizes significant violations of Current Good Manufacturing Practice (CGMP) regulations for medical gases. See Title 21 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR), part 213 (21 CFR part 213). Because your methods, facilities, or controls for manufacturing, processing, packing, or holding do not conform to CGMP, your drug products are adulterated within the meaning of section 501(a)(2)(B) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act), (21 U.S.C. 351(a)(2)(B)). Requirements for Medical Gases Under section 501(a)(2)(B) of the FD&C Act (21 U.S.C. 351(a)(2)(B)), a drug, including a medical gas, is deemed to be adulterated if “the methods used in, or the facilities or controls used for, its manufacture, processing, packing, or holding do not conform to or are not operated or administered in conformity with current good manufacturing practice.” Section 501 of the FD&C Act states that “the term current good manufacturing practice includes the implementation of oversight and controls over the manufacture of drugs to ensure quality, including managing the risk of and establishing the safety of raw materials, materials used in the manufacturing of drugs, and finished drug products.” On June 18, 2024, FDA issued a final rule to take effect on December 18, 2025, revising the requirements concerning CGMP, postmarketing safety reporting, certification, and labeling that apply to certain medical gases. This rule implemented new and revised regulations tailored to medical gases, including CGMP requirements codified in part 213 (21 CFR part 213) and postmarketing quality and safety reporting requirements codified in part 230 (21 CFR part 230). Prior to implementation of these requirements, medical gas manufacturers were subject to the statutory CGMP requirements in section 501(a)(2)(B) of the FD&C Act as well as the regulations for finished pharmaceuticals in parts 210 and 211 (21 CFR parts 210 and 211) and postmarketing quality and safety reporting requirements in part 314 (21 CFR part 314). The requirements codified in parts 213 and 230 are consistent with the prior regulations, including robust quality systems, proper documentation, and timely adverse event reporting, such that the deficiencies observed during the inspection would constitute violations under either regulatory framework. We reviewed your April 15, 2026, response to our Form FDA 483 in detail. Violations of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act The following are violations identified during our inspection and review. As a reminder, this is not an all-inclusive list of violations at your facility. 1. Your firm failed to have, for each batch of medical gas, appropriate laboratory determination of satisfactory conformance to final specifications for the medical gas, including the identity and strength of each active ingredient, prior to release (21 CFR 213.165(a)). 1 Your firm is a manufacturer of Oxygen, USP for administration by inhalation, including for use in hospital settings. Your firm failed to adequately test finished batches of your medical gases for the identity and strength of your active ingredients (Oxygen, USP) before release and distribution, which includes using properly calibrated instruments. For example, while reviewing an investigation into a customer complaint for a medical gas mix-up, our investigator identified that your filling technician reported passing testing results for batches of Oxygen, USP prior to their release without actually performing the required tests. The customer complaint revealed that third-party testing of the Oxygen, USP batches showed the presence of (b)(4) as high as 99% within the containers. A container labeled as medical oxygen administered to a patient despite having a level of 99% (b)(4) (and less than 1% oxygen) represents a catastrophic, immediately life-threatening event from complete oxygen deprivation. Appropriate release testing, which includes strength and identity testing of the active ingredient, must be performed before drug product batch release and distribution. Without adequate testing, you do not have adequate scientific evidence to assure that your medical gases conform to appropriate specifications before release. Further, a second person verification (witness) of all critical testing and adequate review of the testing results by the quality unit prior to release of the drug products should be documented to ensure accuracy and accountability. In your response, you state that you are in the process of developing and implementing comprehensive standard operating procedures (SOPs) with the relocation to your new facility, including procedures for testing and release for distribution. Additionally, you state that you are updating your fill logs to include a second-person verification and plan to record all testing results to enhance the accountability of the testing. Your response is inadequate because you failed to provide your finished product specifications for Oxygen, USP, procedures for medical gas testing and release, evidence of proper calibration of your testing instruments, or testing results to demonstrate that your firm can manufacture medical gases that meet all quality attributes. In response to this letter, provide: A list of all test methods and specifications used to analyze each batch of your drug product before making a batch disposition decision, and the associated written procedures. A comprehensive, independent assessment of your laboratory practices, procedures, methods, equipment, documentation, and analyst competencies. Based on this review, provide a detailed plan to remediate and evaluate the effectiveness of your laboratory system. 2. Your firm failed to test samples of each incoming designated medical gas for identity and conformity with all appropriate written specifications for purity, strength, and quality. Your firm also failed to validate and establish the reliability of your incoming designated medical gas supplier’s test analyses at appropriate intervals (21 CFR 213.82(a) and 213.82(b)). 2 Your firm failed to conduct identity testing for each incoming designated medical gas (DMG) lot used in medical gas manufacturing, including Oxygen, USP. Additionally, you relied on your supplier’s certificates of analysis (COA) of your incoming DMG without establishing the reliability of your supplier’s test analyses at appropriate intervals. CGMP requires identity testing for each DMG lot used in medical gas manufacturing, and you can only rely on the COA for other DMG attributes if you also appropriately validate the supplier’s testing results at appropriate intervals. In your response, you state that you are in the process of developing and implementing comprehensive SOPs as part of the relocation to your new facility, including procedures for control of incoming medical gases as well as supplier qualification and vendor audits. Additionally, you state that you will initiate (b)(4) vendor audits to ensure supplier compliance with applicable quality and regulatory requirements. Your response is inadequate because you have not provided your specifications for your incoming DMG, procedures for testing and release of incoming DMG, evidence of proper calibration of testing instruments, or testing results to demonstrate that your firm can test your incoming DMG to ensure that they meet all quality attributes prior to use in medical gas manufacturing. In your response to this letter, provide: A comprehensive, independent review of your material system, including but not limited to: o Evaluating all suppliers of materials (DMGs, containers, and closures) to determine if they are reliable and appropriately qualified o An assessment of all materials to determine whether they are consistently of acceptable quality o A review to ensure assigned expiration or retest dates are appropriate (supported by data) o Adequacy of the supplier qualification program, and its selection, qualification, and disqualification provisions Based on a thorough review, provide a summary of your system’s corrective action and preventive action (CAPA) to remediate the vendor qualification program and prevent use of unsuitable DMGs, containers and closures. All quality control specifications you use to test and release each incoming lot of DMGs for use in manufacturing. A description of how you will test each DMG lot for conformity with all appropriate specifications for identity, strength, quality, and purity. If you intend to accept any results from your supplier’s COA instead of testing each DMG lot for strength, quality, and purity, specify how you will robustly establish the reliability of your supplier’s results through initial validation as well as periodic revalidation. In addition, include a commitment to always conduct at least one specific identity test for each incoming DMG lot. A summary of results obtained from testing all DMG to evaluate the reliability of the COA from each DMG manufacturer. Include your SOP that describes this COA validation program. A summary of your program for qualifying and overseeing contract facilities that test the DMGs and medical gases you manufacture. An independent, comprehensive review of your material system to determine whether all suppliers of DMGs, containers, and closures, are appropriately qualified; materials are of consistently acceptable quality; and appropriate expiration or retest dates are assigned. Based on this systemic review, provide a summary of a systemic CAPA that remediates your vendor qualification program and prevents use of unsuitable DMGs, containers, and closures. 3. Your firm failed to establish and follow adequate written procedures describing the handling of all written and oral complaints regarding a medical gas, including provisions for review by the quality control unit of any complaint involving the possible failure of a medical gas to meet any of its specifications and, for such medical gas, a determination as to the need for an investigation in accordance with 21 CFR 213.192 (21 CFR 213.198(a)). 3 A hospital contacted your firm in October 2025 to report the presence of (b)(4) in containers of Oxygen, USP that you filled and distributed to them. You stated to our investigator that you told the complainant it was impossible to have (b)(4) in the oxygen tank and subsequently failed to document and investigate the incident in a timely manner per your complaint handling procedure. It was not until after the complainant conducted third-party testing on the contents of the containers and sent you a termination of services letter on November 20, 2025, that you initiated an investigation into the complaint. Your firm’s investigations into the errant Oxygen, USP containers were deficient. Your firm’s investigations revealed that the errant Oxygen, USP containers were filled with (b)(4) during repair by a third party, but upon receipt by your firm, your filling technician failed to test the lot as required. However, your investigations did not consider other containers repaired by the third party; other Oxygen, USP batches that may be affected by the incident; or remediations beyond employee termination and additional employee training. Additionally, you received a complaint from a different hospital about batches of high-pressure Oxygen, USP that contained liquid (e.g., water). Your firm’s investigation into the incident was inconclusive regarding the source of the water and hypothesized that the new equipment with your relocation would be sufficient to (b)(4) any residual water. Your investigation failed to consider incoming DMGs or process-related water sources; other finished Oxygen, USP batches that may be affected by the incident; or corrections that would be appropriate to remediate the cause of the incident. The presence of condensation or water in medical grade oxygen (high-pressure cylinders/tanks) can pose multiple potential risks to patients, including microbial growth, aspiration of aerosolized water droplets, particulate exposure due to internal corrosion, and/or obstruction of oxygen flow. In your response, you state that you are in the process of developing and implementing comprehensive SOPs as part of the relocation to your new facility, including procedures for complaint files, as well as CAPA. Additionally, you state that you have scheduled an interview with the third party that repairs your medical gas containers to finish the complaint investigation into the mix-up incident. Your response is inadequate because you failed to provide sufficient details for how you intend to handle complaints and implement appropriate CAPA. You also did not provide adequate details of your expanded investigations into the complaint incidents related to other batches of medical gases that may be affected, consideration of other sources of the manufacturing defects, and identification of adequate CAPA plans. In your response to this letter, provide: A comprehensive, independent assessment of your overall system for investigating deviations, discrepancies, complaints, out-of-specification results, and failures. Provide a detailed action plan to remediate this system. Your action plan should include, but not be limited to, significant improvements in investigation competencies, scope determination, root cause evaluation, CAPA effectiveness, quality unit oversight, and written procedures. Address how your firm will ensure all phases of investigations are appropriately conducted. An independent, retrospective review of all critical investigations (including each in-process, release, and stability test specification failure) for the last three years as of the date of this letter. Evaluate the adequacy of each investigation, including but not limited to: o Determine whether a thorough review of production (e.g., batch manufacturing records, adequacy of the manufacturing steps, suitability of equipment/facilities, variability of raw materials, process capability, deviation history, complaint history, batch failure history) was conducted. o Assess sufficiency of review of related data and investigations to identify if there are potential systemic linkages. o Evaluate adequacy of scope, rigor, staff competencies, scientific/analytical foundation, root cause determinations, and CAPA. o Summary of findings of the assessment for each of the above elements. An independent assessment and remediation plan for your CAPA program. Provide a report that evaluates whether the program includes effective root cause analysis, ensures CAPA effectiveness, analyzes investigations trends, improves the CAPA program whenever needed, ensures final quality unit decision authority, and is fully supported by executive management. 4. Your firm’s quality unit failed to exercise its responsibility to ensure medical gases are manufactured in compliance with CGMP, and meet established specifications for identity, strength, quality, and purity (21 CFR 213.22). 4 Your firm failed to establish an adequate quality unit (QU) with the responsibilities and authority to oversee the manufacture of medical gases. For example, you failed to ensure: Assignment of an adequate QU with sufficient responsibilities and authorities (213.22(a)). Establishment of appropriate written procedures for medical gas manufacturing (213.22(c)). Personnel training in CGMP requirements with sufficient frequency (213.25(a)). Your QU fundamentally failed to oversee manufacturing procedures, practices, and manufacturing operations. In addition, even when a QU consists of one or only a few persons, those persons are still accountable for ensuring the ongoing effectiveness of all systems and procedures, and for reviewing manufacturing results to ensure a state of control and adherence to all quality standards. In your response, you state that you are in the process of developing and implementing comprehensive SOPs as part of the relocation to your new facility, including quality control procedures, training programs and requirements. Additionally, you state that you are establishing a structured process for conducting internal audits and implementing (b)(4) reviews of production activities and associated documentation to ensure ongoing compliance, identify gaps proactively, and drive continuous improvement. Your response is inadequate because you failed to provide sufficient detail or evidence of corrective actions taken that will ensure your QU maintains proper oversight of your firm’s operations. Additionally, you failed to include details of how your personnel are adequately trained to perform their assigned functions, including CGMP requirements. Significant findings in this letter demonstrate that your firm does not operate an effective quality system in accordance with CGMP. In addition to the lack of effective management oversight of your production and laboratory operations, we found your QU is not enabled to exercise proper authority and/or has insufficiently implemented its responsibilities. Executive management should immediately and comprehensively assess your company’s global manufacturing operations to ensure that your systems, processes, and products conform to FDA requirements. Your firm’s quality systems are inadequate. See FDA’s guidance document Medical Gases—Current Good Manufacturing Practice at https://www.fda.gov/media/70973/download. In your response to this letter, provide: A comprehensive assessment and remediation plan to ensure your QU is given the authority and resources to effectively function. The assessment should also include, but not be limited to: o A determination of whether procedures used by your firm are robust and appropriate o Provisions for QU oversight throughout your operations to evaluate adherence to appropriate practices o A complete and final review of each batch and its related information before the QU disposition decision o Oversight and approval of investigations and discharging of all other QU duties to ensure identity, strength, quality, and purity of all products o Also describe how top management supports quality assurance and reliable operations, including but not limited to timely provision of resources to proactively address emerging manufacturing/quality issues and to assure a continuing state of control A comprehensive assessment of documentation systems used throughout your manufacturing and laboratory operations to determine where documentation practices are insufficient. Include a detailed CAPA plan that comprehensively remediates your firm’s documentation practices to ensure you retain attributable, legible, complete, original, accurate, contemporaneous records throughout your operation. Data Integrity Remediation Your quality system does not adequately ensure the accuracy and integrity of data to support the safety, effectiveness, and quality of the drugs you manufacture. It may be helpful to refer to FDA’s guidance document Data Integrity and Compliance With Drug CGMP: Questions and Answers for guidance on establishing and following CGMP compliant data integrity practices at https://www.fda.gov/media/119267/download. We strongly recommend that you retain an independent, qualified third-party consultant to assist in your remediation. In response to this letter, provide: A comprehensive investigation into the extent of the inaccuracies and inconsistencies in data, records, and reporting. Your investigation should include: o A detailed investigation protocol and methodology; a summary of all laboratories, manufacturing operations, and systems to be covered by the assessment; and a justification for any part of your operation that you propose to exclude. o Interviews of current and former employees to identify the nature, scope, and root cause of data inaccuracies. We recommend that these interviews be conducted by a qualified third party. o An assessment of the extent of data integrity deficiencies at your facility. Identify omissions, alterations, deletions, record destruction, non-contemporaneous record completion, and other deficiencies. Describe all parts of your facility’s operations in which you discovered data integrity deficiencies. o A comprehensive retrospective evaluation of the nature of the data integrity deficiencies. We recommend that a qualified third party with specific expertise in the area where potential breaches were identified should evaluate all occurrences. A current risk assessment of the potential effects of the observed failures on the quality of your drugs. Your assessment should include analyses of the risks to patients caused by the release of drugs affected by a data integrity event and analyses of the risks posed by ongoing operations. A management strategy for your firm that includes the details of your global CAPA plan. Your strategy should include: o A detailed corrective action plan that describes how you intend to ensure the reliability and completeness of all data, including analytical data, manufacturing records, and all data submitted to FDA. o A comprehensive description of the root causes of each data integrity deviation, including evidence that the scope and depth of the current action plan is commensurate with the findings of the investigation and risk assessment. Indicate whether individuals responsible for the data integrity breaches remain able to influence CGMP-related data at your firm. o Interim measures describing the actions you have taken or will take to ensure the quality of your drugs and protect patients, such as notifying your customers, recalling product(s), conducting additional testing, adding lots to your stability programs to assure stability, and enhanced complaint monitoring. o Long-term measures describing any remediation efforts and enhancements to procedures, processes, methods, controls, systems, management oversight, and human resources (e.g., training, staffing improvements) designed to ensure the integrity of your company’s data. o A commitment to have a qualified consultant conduct extensive annual audits, for at least two years, to assist in evaluating CAPA effectiveness after you have executed your data integrity remediation protocol. o Inform FDA if you will be hiring a Chief Integrity Officer who is fully empowered to receive anonymous complaints from employees reporting data integrity concerns and with the authority to ensure any potential breach is promptly investigated (by an independent quality assurance function, along with expertise from outside entities whenever needed). o A status report for any of the above activities already underway or completed. Drug Production Status Given the concerning state of your manufacturing and testing controls for medical grade gases, the unacceptable patient risks posed by your product defects, and the fact that the majority of your operations are unrelated to medical grade gases, in response to this letter, clarify whether you intend to continue to manufacture drugs (e.g., medical gases) for the U.S. market at this facility. If you plan to continue CGMP activities, you are responsible for resolving all deficiencies and systemic flaws to ensure your firm is capable of ongoing CGMP compliance. In addition, based upon the nature of the violations we identified at your firm, you should engage a consultant qualified as set forth in 21 CFR 213.34 to assist your firm in meeting CGMP requirements. The qualified consultant should also perform a comprehensive six-system audit of your entire operation for CGMP compliance and evaluate the completion and efficacy of all CAPA, before you pursue resolution of your firm’s compliance status with FDA. In your response to this letter, provide a summary of your remediations to demonstrate that you have appropriately completed all CAPA. Conclusion As previously stated, you are responsible for investigating and determining the root causes of any violations and implementing corrective and preventative measures to ensure future and sustained compliance so that these violations and any others do not occur. Unresolved violations may prevent other Federal agencies from awarding contracts. Failure to address violations may also cause FDA to withhold issuance of Export Certificates. FDA may withhold approval of new applications or supplements listing your firm as a drug manufacturer until any violations are completely addressed and we confirm your compliance with CGMP. We may re-inspect to verify that you have completed corrective actions to address any violations. Send your written response to CDER-OC-OMQ-Communications@fda.hhs.gov within fifteen (15) business days of receipt of this letter. Identify your written response with FEI 1625647 and ATTN: Philip Kreiter in the letter. If you have information that you believe demonstrates that your products are not in violation of the FD&C Act and FDA regulations, include that information for our consideration. Please note FDA posts warning letters on www.FDA.gov. Sincerely, /S/ Francis Godwin Director Office of Manufacturing Quality Office of Compliance Center for Drug Evaluation and Research U.S. Food and Drug Administration ______________________ 1 See also 21 CFR 211.165(a) 2 See also 21 CFR 211.84(d). 3 See also 21 CFR 211.198(a). 4 See also 21 CFR 211.22. key_violations.citation: section 301(e) of the FD&C Act (21 U.S.C. 331(e))
key_violations.original: On May 1, 2026, FDA sent an initial electronic request for records and other information pursuant to section 704(a)(4) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act), 21 U.S.C. 374(a)(4), to the contact e-mail address provided in your registration file and to your U.S. Agent. This request went unanswered as did numerous follow-up requests, including a second electronic request sent on May 19, 2026, and a separate phone call to the listed U.S. Agent of record on May 27, 2026. Additionally, FDA sent a follow-up written request for such records and other information by United Parcel Service (UPS) on May 28, 2026. Delivery of the UPS package was confirmed by signature of your facility representative, but you failed to respond to any of these attempted communications or otherwise provide the requested records or other information. Pursuant to section 704(a)(4), FDA’s request and follow-up communication included a sufficient and clear description of the records sought. It is a prohibited act under section 301(e) of the FD&C Act (21 U.S.C. 331(e)) to refuse to permit access to or copying of any record as required by section 704(a).
key_violations.description: 2026년 5월 1일 FDA 는 연방 식품·의약품·화장품법(FD&C Act) 제704(a)(4)조(21 U.S.C. 374(a)(4))에 따른 기록 및 기타 정보에 대한 최초 전자 요청을 귀사 등록 파일에 기재된 연락 이메일 주소와 귀사의 미국 대리인에게 보냈다. 이 요청은 회신되지 않았으며, 2026년 5월 19일 보낸 두 번째 전자 요청과 2026년 5월 27일 등록된 미국 대리인에게 한 별도 전화를 포함한 여러 후속 요청도 마찬가지였다. 또한 FDA 는 2026년 5월 28일 UPS(United Parcel Service)를 통해 해당 기록과 정보에 대한 후속 서면 요청을 보냈다. UPS 소포의 배송은 귀사 시설 담당자의 서명으로 확인됐으나, 귀사는 이러한 연락 시도 어느 것에도 응답하지 않았고 요청된 기록이나 정보를 제공하지도 않았다. 제704(a)(4)조에 따라 FDA 의 요청과 후속 연락에는 요구하는 기록에 대한 충분하고 명확한 설명이 포함돼 있었다. 제704(a)조에서 요구하는 기록에 대한 접근이나 복사를 허용하지 않는 것은 FD&C Act 제301(e)조(21 U.S.C. 331(e))에 따른 금지행위다.
key_violations.risk: 기록 제출 거부로 품질보증 수준을 확인할 수 없어 해당 제조소 제품 전체가 수입 차단 대상이 된다.

key_violations.original: Specifically, your “XUEYI SKIN CARE” sunscreen drug product contains the cancelled color additive CI 11680 (also known as Ext. D&C Yellow No. 5 1 ). In 1966, FDA cancelled the certification and delisted Ext D&C Yellow No. 5 due to lack of safety data from any manufacturer. Under 21 CFR 81.30(d), using Ext D&C Yellow No. 5 after October 4, 1966, results in the drug being adulterated. Your use of a cancelled color additive in your drug product formulation renders it adulterated under 501(a)(4)(A).
key_violations.description: 구체적으로, 귀사의 “XUEYI SKIN CARE” 자외선차단제 의약품에는 취소된 색소 첨가물 CI 11680(Ext. D&C Yellow No. 5 로도 알려짐 1 )이 함유돼 있다. FDA 는 1966년 어떤 제조업체로부터도 안전성 자료가 없다는 이유로 Ext D&C Yellow No. 5 의 인증을 취소하고 목록에서 삭제했다. 21 CFR 81.30(d) 에 따라 1966년 10월 4일 이후 Ext D&C Yellow No. 5 를 사용하면 그 의약품은 불량의약품(adulterated)이 된다. 귀사가 의약품 처방에 취소된 색소를 사용한 것은 그 제품을 501(a)(4)(A) 에 따른 불량의약품으로 만든다.
key_violations.risk: 안전성 자료가 없는 색소가 피부 도포 제품에 사용돼 제품 자체가 불량의약품이 된다.

key_violations.original: Based on information from FDA import records, there appear to be discrepancies in the electronic import entry submissions for your products, specifically regarding the failure to correctly declare your drug product listing. Prior to distributing products intended for the United States, you should ensure that the firms shipping or importing your drug products, and the entry filers transmitting the electronic data to U.S. Customs and Border Protection and FDA, are declaring your firm as the manufacturer, as well as using your registration number and product listing number(s). See 21 CFR 1.74(a)(1).
key_violations.description: FDA 수입 기록 정보에 따르면, 귀사 제품의 전자 수입 신고 제출 내용에 불일치가 있는 것으로 보이며, 특히 귀사 의약품 품목 리스팅을 정확히 신고하지 않은 점이 그렇다. 미국용 제품을 유통하기 전에, 귀사 의약품을 선적하거나 수입하는 업체와 미국 관세국경보호청(CBP) 및 FDA 에 전자 데이터를 전송하는 신고 대행자가 귀사를 제조소로 신고하고 귀사의 등록번호와 품목 리스팅 번호를 사용하는지 확인해야 한다. 21 CFR 1.74(a)(1) 참조.
key_violations.risk: 수입 신고상 제조소·품목 정보가 틀리면 추적성이 무너지고 반입 거부·억류 위험이 커진다.

deep_analysis.fda_evaluation: 업체가 여러 차례의 704(a)(4) 요청과 연락 시도에 전혀 응답하지 않아 FDA 가 평가할 회신 자체가 없었다. FDA 는 이 때문에 이 시설에서 제조된 것으로 등재된 의약품의 품질보증 수준을 알 수 있는 근거가 없다고 밝혔고, 2026년 7월 31일 이 업체의 모든 의약품을 Import Alert 66-79 에 등재했다. 서한은 회신 시 FDA 실사 일정 요청을 제출할 수 있다고 안내했다.

required_remediation.deadline: 서한 수령 후 15영업일(working days) 이내 서면 회신(CDER-OC-OMQ-Communications@fda.hhs.gov)
items: 704(a)(4) 요청에 따른 기록과 정보를 제출하고, 필요 시 FDA 실사 일정을 요청한다.
의약품 처방에서 취소된 색소(CI 11680 등)를 제거하고 색소의 규제 상태를 검토한다.
수입자·신고 대행자가 자사를 제조소로, 등록번호·품목 리스팅 번호를 정확히 신고하도록 조치한다.
화장품 제품에 대해서도 FD&C Act 와 MoCRA 요건 준수를 확인한다.

deep_analysis.administrative_risks: FDA 가 CGMP 및 기타 요건 준수를 확인할 수 있을 때까지 이 업체를 제조소로 기재한 신규 신청·변경 승인이 보류될 수 있다. 또한 불량 또는 부정표시로 보이는 이 업체 제조품의 미국 선적분은 FD&C Act 801(a)(3) 에 따라 억류되거나 반입이 거부될 수 있으며, 취소 색소 함유 제품의 주간 거래 도입은 301(a) 금지행위에 해당한다.

91bceac3ffe8.source_text: FDA Review Violations were identified and documented during review of your drug manufacturing facility, Guangdong Bisutang Biotechnology Co., Ltd., FDA Establishment Identifier (FEI) 3031796296. This review was conducted under FDA’s statutory authority and public health responsibilities to protect the public from unsafe, ineffective, and poor quality drugs. Your facility is registered with the FDA as a manufacturer of over-the-counter (OTC) drug products, including sunscreen. A review of import records showed multiple shipments of products into the United States, which declared Guangdong Bisutang Biotechnology Co., Ltd., as the manufacturer. On May 1, 2026, FDA sent an initial electronic request for records and other information pursuant to section 704(a)(4) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act), 21 U.S.C. 374(a)(4), to the contact e-mail address provided in your registration file and to your U.S. Agent. This request went unanswered as did numerous follow-up requests, including a second electronic request sent on May 19, 2026, and a separate phone call to the listed U.S. Agent of record on May 27, 2026. Additionally, FDA sent a follow-up written request for such records and other information by United Parcel Service (UPS) on May 28, 2026. Delivery of the UPS package was confirmed by signature of your facility representative, but you failed to respond to any of these attempted communications or otherwise provide the requested records or other information. Pursuant to section 704(a)(4), FDA’s request and follow-up communication included a sufficient and clear description of the records sought. It is a prohibited act under section 301(e) of the FD&C Act (21 U.S.C. 331(e)) to refuse to permit access to or copying of any record as required by section 704(a). Because your firm failed to respond to the section 704(a)(4) records requests and associated communication attempts, we have no indication of the level of quality assurance for drugs listed as manufactured at your facility. FDA placed all drugs and drug products offered for import into the United States from your firm on Import Alert 66-79 on July 31, 2026. Use of Cancelled Color Additive Ext. D&C Yellow No. 5 Based on your drug product listing we determined that your “XUEYI SKIN CARE” sunscreen is adulterated under section 501(a)(4)(A) of the FD&C Act as this FDA-listed drug product bears or contains a color additive that is unsafe within the meaning of section 721 of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 379e. Specifically, your “XUEYI SKIN CARE” sunscreen drug product contains the cancelled color additive CI 11680 (also known as Ext. D&C Yellow No. 5 1 ). In 1966, FDA cancelled the certification and delisted Ext D&C Yellow No. 5 due to lack of safety data from any manufacturer. Under 21 CFR 81.30(d), using Ext D&C Yellow No. 5 after October 4, 1966, results in the drug being adulterated. Your use of a cancelled color additive in your drug product formulation renders it adulterated under 501(a)(4)(A). Accordingly, the introduction or delivery for introduction of “XUEYI SKIN CARE” sunscreen into interstate commerce is a prohibited act under section 301(a) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 331(a). For more information regarding color nomenclature see the webpage for Regulatory Status of Color Additives at: https://www.hfpappexternal.fda.gov/scripts/fdcc/index.cfm?set=ColorAdditives. Drug Import Information You manufacture both drug and cosmetic products. Based on information from FDA import records, there appear to be discrepancies in the electronic import entry submissions for your products, specifically regarding the failure to correctly declare your drug product listing. Prior to distributing products intended for the United States, you should ensure that the firms shipping or importing your drug products, and the entry filers transmitting the electronic data to U.S. Customs and Border Protection and FDA, are declaring your firm as the manufacturer, as well as using your registration number and product listing number(s). See 21 CFR 1.74(a)(1). Cosmetics Manufactured for Distribution in the United States In addition, some of the products you manufacture may be regulated as cosmetics, as defined in section 201(i) of the FD&C Act (21 U.S.C. 321(i)). Any cosmetics you manufacture must comply with applicable statutory and regulatory requirements, including the FD&C Act. We note that under section 301(a) of the FD&C Act (21 U.S.C. 331(a)), it is a prohibited act to introduce or deliver for introduction into interstate commerce a cosmetic that is adulterated or misbranded. We also note that the Modernization of Cosmetics Regulation Act of 2022 (MoCRA) provides new requirements with which facilities that manufacture cosmetic products must comply. You may find the FD&C Act, MoCRA, and FDA’s regulations through links on FDA’s website at www.fda.gov. Conclusion FDA placed all drugs and drug products offered for import into the United States from your firm on Import Alert 66-79 on July 31, 2026. Until FDA is able to confirm compliance with CGMP and other applicable requirements, we may withhold approval of any new applications or supplements listing your firm as a drug manufacturer. In addition, shipments of articles manufactured at Guangdong Bisutang Biotechnology Co., Ltd., at Floor 1-5, One of No. 15 (Factory Building 1-1), Industrial Cluster Development Zone, Xiamao Town, Zhaoqing into the United States that appear to be adulterated or misbranded are subject to being detained or refused admission pursuant to section 801(a)(3) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 381(a)(3). After you receive this letter, respond to this office in writing within 15 working days. In response to this letter, you may submit a request to schedule an FDA inspection. Send your written response to CDER-OC-OMQ-Communications@fda.hhs.gov. Identify your written response with FEI 3031796296 and ATTN: Lynnsey Renn in the letter or in the subject line of the email. If you have information that you believe demonstrates that your products are not in violation of the FD&C Act and FDA regulations, include that information for our consideration. FDA posts warning letters to www.FDA.gov. Sincerely, /S/ Francis Godwin Director Office of Manufacturing Quality Office of Compliance Center for Drug Evaluation and Research U.S. Food and Drug Administration cc: Faye Liang & Clare Ho US Agent (b)(4) _________________________ 1 Not to be confused with the similar sounding but listed color additive Food, Drug, and Cosmetic (FD&C) Yellow 5 Content current as of: 11/03/2026 Regulated Product(s) Drugs Feedback FDA Archive About FDA Accessibility Visitor Information Website Policies / Privacy No FEAR Act Vulnerability Disclosure Policy FOIA HHS.gov USA.gov Contact FDA Follow FDA on Facebook Follow FDA on X Follow FDA on Instagram Follow FDA on LinkedIn View FDA videos on YouTube Subscribe to FDA RSS feeds Contact Number 1-888-INFO-FDA (1-888-463-6332) Back to Top

key_violations.original: 자사 기준서에서 ‘작업자는 제조공정과 동시에 해당 내용을 기록한다.’, '‘제조(포장)지시 및 기록서’ 제조(포장)기록의 세부항목은 제조(포장)작업과 동시에 기록되어야 한다.’라고 규정하고 있음에도 불구하고, 수탁 제조하는 품목에 대하여 해당 제품 포장지시 및 기록서에 1차 포장, 2차 포장 작업에 대한 일부 기록을 수행하지 않은 것이 확인되는 등 자사 기준서를 미준수한 사실이 있음
key_violations.description: 자사 기준서는 작업자가 제조공정과 동시에 내용을 기록하고, 제조(포장)기록의 세부항목을 제조(포장)작업과 동시에 기록하도록 규정했으나, 수탁 제조 품목의 포장지시 및 기록서에 1차 포장·2차 포장 작업의 일부 기록을 수행하지 않아 자사 기준서를 지키지 않았다.
key_violations.risk: 포장 작업 기록이 비어 있으면 포장 공정의 실제 수행 여부와 혼동·오포장 가능성을 사후에 검증할 수 없어 배치 출하 판정의 근거가 약해진다.

key_violations.citation: ｢의약품 등의 제조업 및 수입자의 시설기준령 시행규칙｣ 제11조제3항제2호
key_violations.original: ○ 수탁자 준수사항 위반(기준서 미준수)
key_violations.description: 처분 사유는 수탁자로서 지켜야 할 준수사항 위반, 구체적으로 기준서 미준수로 분류됐다.
key_violations.risk: 수탁자의 기록 결함은 위탁자 품목의 품질 책임으로 이어져 위탁·수탁 양측의 품질협약 이행이 함께 문제 된다.

deep_analysis.disposition_basis: 처분은 해당 제형(첩부제) 제조업무정지 15일(2026. 11. 18. ~ 2026. 12. 2.)이다. 처분 근거로 ｢약사법｣ 제76조와 ｢의약품 등의 안전에 관한 규칙｣ 제95조 관련 [별표 8] 행정처분의 기준 Ⅱ. 개별기준 제2호 자목 2) 나)가 적용됐으며, 위반 법령으로는 ｢약사법｣ 제31조제1항, ｢의약품 등의 제조업 및 수입자의 시설기준령｣ 제4조, 같은 시행규칙 제11조제3항제2호가 제시됐다. 처분 범위가 개별 품목이 아니라 제형 전체라는 점이 특징이다.

items: 업무정지 기간 동안 첩부제 제형의 제조 업무를 중단한다.
수탁 제조 품목의 포장지시 및 기록서에서 1차·2차 포장 기록 누락 범위를 소급 확인한다.
작업과 동시 기록 원칙이 지켜지도록 포장 현장 기록 방식과 기록 검토 절차를 보완한다.
위탁자에게 기록 결함 사실과 시정 내용을 공유한다.

deep_analysis.administrative_risks: 같은 기준서 미준수가 반복되면 [별표 8] 행정처분 기준에 따라 가중된 처분을 받을 수 있고, 후속 GMP 실사에서 기록 관리 전반이 재점검될 가능성이 있다. 수탁 제조 업체인 만큼 위탁자와의 계약·품질협약 관계에도 영향이 있을 수 있다.

○ 수탁자 준수사항 위반(기준서 미준수)
자사 기준서에서 ‘작업자는 제조공정과 동시에 해당 내용을 기록한다.’, '‘제조(포장)지시 및 기록서’ 제조(포장)기록의 세부항목은 제조(포장)작업과 동시에 기록되어야 한다.’라고 규정하고 있음에도 불구하고, 수탁 제조하는 품목에 대하여 해당 제품 포장지시 및 기록서에 1차 포장, 2차 포장 작업에 대한 일부 기록을 수행하지 않은 것이 확인되는 등 자사 기준서를 미준수한 사실이 있음

key_violations.description: 큐레이드(벤잘코늄염화물반창고(1회용)) 등 제품을 수거·검사한 결과 형상(폭)과 인장강도 시험항목이 부적합으로 나타났다.
key_violations.risk: 반창고의 폭·인장강도가 규격을 벗어나면 부착·보호 기능이 떨어져 사용 중 탈락이나 상처 보호 실패로 이어질 수 있다.

key_violations.original:
처분명: 해당 품목 제조업무정지 15일(2026.11.18.~2026.12.2.)
*해당품목: 큐레이드(벤잘코늄염화물반창고(1회용)), 아쿠아밴드멸균형
key_violations.description: 처분은 해당 품목인 큐레이드(벤잘코늄염화물반창고(1회용))와 아쿠아밴드멸균형에 대한 제조업무정지 15일(2026.11.18.~2026.12.2.)이다.
key_violations.risk: 유통 단계 수거·검사에서 부적합이 확인된 만큼 시중 유통 배치 전반의 품질 신뢰가 문제 된다.

deep_analysis.disposition_basis: 처분은 해당 품목(큐레이드(벤잘코늄염화물반창고(1회용)), 아쿠아밴드멸균형) 제조업무정지 15일(2026.11.18.~2026.12.2.)이다. 위반 법령은 약사법 제62조 제11호 및 같은 법 제66조이며, 처분은 「약사법」 제76조 제1항 제4호 및 「의약품 등의 안전에 관한 규칙」 제95조 [별표8] 행정처분의 기준 Ⅱ. 개별기준 제39호 가목 11) 규정에 따른 것이다. 근거는 수거·검사에서 확인된 형상(폭)·인장강도 시험항목 부적합이다.

items: 업무정지 기간 동안 대상 2개 품목의 제조 업무를 중단한다.
형상(폭)·인장강도 부적합의 원인을 원단·재단·제조 공정 단위로 조사한다.
출하 시험에서 형상(폭)·인장강도 항목의 측정·판정이 배치마다 이뤄지는지 점검하고 보완한다.

deep_analysis.administrative_risks: 재수거·검사에서 같은 시험항목 부적합이 다시 확인되면 [별표8] 개별기준에 따라 가중된 처분을 받을 수 있고, 해당 품목의 유통 배치에 대한 회수 조치가 함께 요구될 가능성이 있다.

key_violations.original:
- 의약품 제조업자는「약사법」제62조제3호에 따라, 기준이 정하여진 의약품(한약재)으로서 정한 기준에 맞지 아니한 의약품을 판매할 목적으로 제조하여서는 아니 되나,
 - ‘다온목단피(제조번호: DO-38-2508)’의 품질검사 결과, 이산화항의 기준이 초과한 제품을 제조하여 판매한 사실이 있음
   *  (기준) 30ppm이하 / (결과) 540ppm
key_violations.description: 의약품 제조업자는 「약사법」 제62조제3호에 따라 기준이 정해진 한약재로서 그 기준에 맞지 않는 의약품을 판매할 목적으로 제조해서는 안 되지만, 다온목단피(제조번호: DO-38-2508)의 품질검사 결과 이산화황(원문 표기 '이산화항') 기준을 초과한 제품을 제조해 판매했다. 기준은 30ppm 이하, 결과는 540ppm 이었다.
key_violations.risk: 이산화황이 기준을 크게 넘는 한약재가 유통되면 복용자에게 과민반응 등 안전 위험이 생길 수 있고, 원료 입고·출하 판정 체계의 실효성이 부정된다.

deep_analysis.disposition_basis: 처분은 해당 품목(다온목단피) 제조업무정지 3개월(2026. 11. 17. ~ 2027. 2. 16.)이다. 적용법령은 「약사법」제62조제3호 및 「의약품 등의 안전에 관한 규칙」제95조 관련 [별표8]Ⅱ.개별기준 제39호라목11호이다. 기준 대비 결과값의 초과 폭이 크고 해당 제품이 실제로 판매됐다는 사실이 처분 근거로 제시됐다.

items: 업무정지 기간 동안 다온목단피 품목의 제조 업무를 중단한다.
제조번호 DO-38-2508 외 다른 제조번호에 대해서도 이산화황 시험 결과를 소급 검토한다.
한약재 원료 입고 및 완제 출하 단계의 이산화황 시험·판정 절차를 보완한다.
기준을 초과한 제품이 유통된 범위를 파악하고 필요한 회수 조치를 검토한다.

deep_analysis.administrative_risks: 같은 위반이 반복되면 [별표8] 개별기준에 따라 처분이 가중되며, 품목허가 취소 등 상위 처분으로 이어질 수 있다. 기준 초과 제품이 판매된 사실이 확인된 만큼 후속 수거·검사가 강화될 가능성이 있다.

key_violations.original:
- 의약품 제조업자는 의약품 제조 시 의약품 제조 및 품질관리기준  준수하여 자사 기준서 ‘불만처리 규정(문서번호: KBP-G021)’에 따라, 품질보증부서는 불만 접수 시 작성된 불만조사보고서 또는 불만 보고서를 제조부서 및 품질부서(보증)책임자, 고객불만처리위원회 위원장의 검토를 받아야함에도 불구하고,
 - 동 업체는 ‘글로스타정10밀리그램(아토르바스타틴칼슘수화물)(제조번호: AR003)’에 대하여 접수된 불만을 처리하면서 품질부서책임자가 주관하지 않고 처리한 사실이 있음
key_violations.description: 의약품 제조업자는 의약품 제조 및 품질관리기준을 준수해 자사 기준서 '불만처리 규정(문서번호: KBP-G021)'에 따라, 품질보증부서가 불만 접수 시 작성한 불만조사보고서 또는 불만 보고서를 제조부서 및 품질부서(보증)책임자, 고객불만처리위원회 위원장의 검토를 받아야 하지만, 이 업체는 글로스타정10밀리그램(아토르바스타틴칼슘수화물)(제조번호: AR003)에 접수된 불만을 처리하면서 품질부서책임자가 주관하지 않고 처리했다.
key_violations.risk: 품질책임자의 주관 없이 불만이 종결되면 제품 결함 가능성이 품질 판단 없이 묻혀 회수·CAPA 착수가 늦어질 수 있다.

key_violations.original: ○ 의약품 제조업자의 준수사항 등의 규정 위반
key_violations.description: 위반은 의약품 제조업자의 준수사항 등의 규정 위반으로 분류됐다.
key_violations.risk: GMP 준수사항 위반으로 분류돼 품질시스템 전반의 이행 신뢰가 문제 된다.

deep_analysis.disposition_basis: 처분은 해당 품목(글로스타정10밀리그램(아토르바스타틴칼슘수화물)) 제조업무정지 1개월(2026. 11. 12. ~ 2026. 12. 11.)이다. 위반 근거는 「약사법」제38조제1항 및 「의약품 등의 안전에 관한 규칙」제48조제9호가목[별표1] 의약품 제조 및 품질관리기준이며, 처분은 「약사법」제76조 및 같은 규칙 제95조 관련 [별표8]Ⅱ.개별기준 제25호다목3)에 따른 것이다. 불만 처리 결과가 아니라 처리 주체·검토 절차의 위반이 처분 사유가 됐다.

items: 업무정지 기간 동안 대상 품목의 제조 업무를 중단한다.
제조번호 AR003 불만 건을 품질부서책임자 주관으로 재검토하고 결론을 재승인한다.
다른 불만 건에서도 불만처리 규정(KBP-G021)이 정한 검토가 빠졌는지 소급 확인한다.
불만 종결 전 필수 검토자 승인을 확인하는 절차를 보완한다.

deep_analysis.administrative_risks: 같은 GMP 준수사항 위반이 반복되면 [별표8] 개별기준에 따라 처분이 가중될 수 있고, 후속 GMP 실사에서 불만처리·품질보증 체계 전반이 재점검될 가능성이 있다.
